title: The waltz joins the band
work: Waltz of the Flowers — principal-waltz passage
question: What happens to Tchaikovsky’s waltz when a concert band takes the place of the strings?
intro: A flourish from the harp clears the floor, and four horns begin the dance. Stokowski’s Philadelphia orchestra and Robinson’s London players keep Tchaikovsky’s scoring, with violins waiting to take over. Lawrence Odom’s concert-band arrangement gives the strings’ work to wind players.

recordings.label: Leopold Stokowski, Philadelphia Orchestra
recordings.note: The Philadelphia Orchestra in Camden’s Trinity Church studio, with the original horn melody and string accompaniment.

recordings.label: Stanford Robinson, National Symphony Orchestra
recordings.note: London’s National Symphony Orchestra plays Tchaikovsky’s scoring, recorded at Kingsway Hall in January 1945.

recordings.label: United States Air Force Band
recordings.note: Lawrence Odom’s concert-band arrangement, recorded for Christmas on Stage and Screen: the winds take on the strings’ parts.

passages.label: The horns begin
passages.note: Four horns sing the first tune above a plucked bass and quiet chords from the strings.

passages.label: The clarinet’s answer
passages.note: The clarinet curls through quick notes between the horns’ phrases; the accompaniment keeps the three-beat dance going.

passages.label: The strings take over
passages.note: The strings carry a fuller melody while brass chords mark the beat and the woodwind add quick flourishes.
